items.title: Windows 11 Is Collecting Data on Which Coding Agents and Developer Tools You Use
items.summary: Windows 11's MissionControlAggregator.dll monitors specific AI coding agents and developer tools via ETW events, recording usage as bitsets in diagnostic reports. This data is saved locally and uploaded to Microsoft unless the user has opted out of optional diagnostic data, which is enabled by default.
items.why_it_matters: The component discards detailed runtime metrics but records which specific agents and tools were observed, creating a privacy exposure regarding developer workflow composition.
items.next_step_detail: Read the analysis and follow the provided steps to disable or block the telemetry DLL.

items.title: OpenCode Browse
items.summary: OpenCode Browse is an MCP server and Chromium extension that allows agents to operate a user's real browser, utilizing existing tabs, logins, and extensions while opening new tabs in the background. It supports actions like reading pages, clicking, typing, and taking screenshots, with a handoff mechanism for interactive steps such as 2FA or payments.
items.why_it_matters: It allows agents to leverage existing user credentials and browser state without requiring separate API keys or setup, while maintaining user control over sensitive interactions.
items.next_step_detail: Install the Chrome extension and run the quick‑start CLI as described on the product page.
items.verification_note: OpenCode Browse has a handoff mechanism for interactive steps such as 2FA or payments

items.title: vstorm-co / agenticos
items.summary: AgenticOS is an open-source, self-hosted platform that allows teams to build, run, and govern AI agents on their own servers and models. It features shared chat, RAG, skills, a real browser, MCP integration, budgets, approvals, and an audit trail.
items.why_it_matters: It provides a layer for running AI teammates on your own infrastructure, enabling teams to manage agent access, cost, and results in one place.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and run the quick‑start Docker compose to spin up a local instance.

items.title: Running coding agents without handing them my credentials
items.summary: The author introduces Lend, a framework that lets remote AI agents invoke local tools on a laptop only after explicit user approval, keeping secrets like SSH keys and 1Password vault safe. Agents run in disposable VMs while the host machine retains privileged credentials and CLI logins.
items.why_it_matters: It provides a practical security pattern for running LLM‑driven coding agents without exposing personal credentials.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the Lend repo and run the quick‑start script to connect a remote agent to your local toolset.

items.title: uBlock Origin's picker flaw and the authorization fix explained
items.summary: uBlock Origin patched a Firefox MV2 vulnerability where a hostile webpage could exploit a resource-serving filter to load the element picker and save trusted filters that execute script in other sites' contexts. The fix requires a verified secret token to launch the picker, as previous request-method hardening was bypassable.
items.why_it_matters: The advisory documents that rules added via the picker are treated as trusted and can inject JavaScript into matching pages, meaning a compromised picker interface allows a hostile page to borrow extension authority to affect other websites.
items.next_step_detail: Update uBlock Origin to version 1.60.0 or later via your package manager or browser extension store.

items.title: isair / jarvis
items.summary: Jarvis is a private, local-first AI assistant for macOS, Windows, and Linux that uses local hardware for speech recognition, language models, and synthesis. It features a rolling transcript for conversational context, a local diary and knowledge graph, and built-in tools like web search and file access.
items.why_it_matters: It allows users to run AI workflows on their own hardware with local data storage, though it requires specific memory budgets for models and relies on the network for external tools like web search.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and run `docker compose up` to launch the assistant locally.

items.title: We measured what AI coding agents preload into their prompts. It wastes 99.6% of context and misses the runtime entity 53% of the time.
items.summary: A peer-verified empirical report demonstrates that naive context preloading in AI agents consumes 272,607 tokens per query with a 0% Turn-0 success rate across 50 enterprise scenarios, whereas a deterministic graph-based resolution layer reduces token usage by 99.2% and achieves 86.7% success. The study identifies that flat retrieval methods fail to resolve multi-instance runtime entities, causing agents to execute against incorrect infrastructure targets.
items.why_it_matters: The data reveals that prompt tuning cannot fix missing runtime entity bindings, indicating that deterministic context resolution is required to prevent agents from executing actions against the wrong database clusters or infrastructure endpoints.
items.next_step_detail: Read the full dev.to article to apply its findings to your own agent prompt templates.

items.title: Optimizely compromised, served malware on Zoom, GitLab
items.summary: A malicious JavaScript campaign was delivered through the Optimizely experimentation platform to 178 organizations, including major sites like Zoom and GitLab, stealing credentials, payment data, and delivering iOS exploits. The attack swapped cryptocurrency wallet addresses and captured screenshots.
items.why_it_matters: If you rely on Optimizely or similar third‑party script platforms, your production front‑ends could be compromised.
items.next_step_detail: Audit any Optimizely integrations, remove the script, and apply the vendor's security advisory.

items.title: An MCP Tool Call Can Resolve and Still Fail

items.title: Strands to Strands over A2A on Bedrock AgentCore, With IAM as the Only Credential
items.summary: A step-by-step guide demonstrates connecting two Strands agents over the Agent2Agent protocol on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime using AWS IAM as the sole credential. The setup requires the caller to sign every request with SigV4, eliminating the need for API keys, OAuth clients, or shared secrets.
items.why_it_matters: It provides a specific implementation where a single IAM identity signs both model calls and agent-to-agent requests, removing the management of separate API keys or shared secrets.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the example repo and run the provided Terraform script to spin up the AgentCore runtime.

items.title: Deploying new Temporal workflow code while workflows are running
items.summary: Deploying non-deterministic changes to running Temporal workflows causes nondeterminism errors that leave workflows stuck in a Running state while retrying failed tasks. The `patched()` function resolves this by allowing new code to skip changes for workflows that have already passed the modification point.
items.why_it_matters: Without using `patched()`, a standard restart or rolling deploy breaks a significant portion of in-flight workflows, and these failures are invisible to dashboards that only count failed workflows.
items.next_step_detail: Read the article and apply the versioning strategy to your existing Temporal deployments.

items.title: The Agentic Loop Explained: Step Through the Plan, Build, Judge and Repeat Loop Behind AI Coding Agents
items.summary: The agentic loop cycles through planning, building, and judging steps to iteratively refine code until a goal is met or a budget is exhausted. A separate judge agent is required to catch specification errors that a builder's self-check might miss, such as incorrect HTTP status codes.
items.why_it_matters: Using an independent judge prevents shipping confident bugs by ensuring the output meets the full specification, not just passing tests.
items.next_step_detail: Read the article to align your agent architecture with the described loop.

items.title: ArXiv: Risk-certified prompt optimization for LLM-as-a-judge guardrails
items.summary: This paper formulates system-prompt selection for LLM-as-a-judge guardrails as a constrained optimization problem that maximizes benign pass rate while keeping the missed-attack rate below a user-specified level with finite-sample statistical control. It introduces two procedures, CPS and CRISP, which use distribution-free risk certification to select prompts that respect target safety levels on held-out tests.
items.why_it_matters: The framework provides a method to ensure LLM-based evaluation pipelines meet explicit safety constraints, such as limiting missed-attack rates, rather than just optimizing for average performance.
items.next_step_detail: Download the PDF and review the optimization formulation.

items.title: HF Paper: LuthorSQL: A One-Pass Text-to-SQL Model as System 1 for a Slower LLM Agent
items.summary: LuthorSQL is a non-autoregressive 7B text-to-SQL model that acts as a rapid System 1 gate for slower LLM agents, predicting slot scores over a bounded grammar to compile and run candidate plans. It achieves 68.03% execution accuracy on BIRD's hidden test set at 0.84 seconds per question on a single GPU and transfers zero-shot to other SQL dialects within 3.1 points of its native accuracy.
items.why_it_matters: By answering nearly half of all questions locally when combined with Claude Opus 5.5, LuthorSQL cuts API costs by 33.3% at the same accuracy while keeping sensitive organizational queries away from external APIs.
items.next_step_detail: Compare LuthorSQL accuracy and latency against your current LLM‑based SQL tool on a sample query set.
